---
title: Build forms from types in a Raycast extension
description: Let a Raycast command save an item of any type, with a form built from the type's fields, and see what Marfa says when the key can't write a type.
---

- **You'll build** a form that changes with the type you choose, built from what Marfa says about the type.
- **You need** the extension from [Build a Raycast extension](/build/raycast-extension), its key, and a terminal with the CLI signed in to your instance.
- **You'll have** a command that saves an item of any type its key can write, and shows the server's refusal for one it can't.

A **type** lists the fields its items hold, and each field says what kind of value it takes. Read the type, and the extension can draw a form for it with no code that knows the type by name. A type you add later gets its form with no change to the extension. [Items and types](/build/items-and-types) explains both.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Read the types

In the extension's folder, add Raycast's utilities, which the form uses to load data:

```bash
npm install @raycast/utils
```

In `src/marfa.ts`, import the client's schema types alongside `createClient`, and add two calls beside `createItem`:

```ts title="src/marfa.ts"
import { createClient, type components } from "@withmarfa/client";

export type TypeDefinition = components["schemas"]["TypeDefinition"];

export async function listTypes() {
  const { data, error, response } = await client().GET("/types");
  if (error) throw refused(response, error);
  return data.data;
}

export async function getType(id: string) {
  const { data, error, response } = await client().GET("/types/{id}", {
    params: { path: { id } },
  });
  if (error) throw refused(response, error);
  return data;
}
```

[List types](/api-reference/types/listTypes) answers the types the instance holds, in `data`. [Get a type](/api-reference/types/getType) answers one with **every field it holds, including the ones it inherits from its parent type**, so a form built from it is complete.

</Step>
<Step>

### Turn a field into a form control

Each field has a kind: text, a number, a date, a yes or no, or one value from a list. Match each kind to a Raycast control:

```tsx title="src/fields.tsx"
import { Form } from "@raycast/api";
import type { TypeDefinition } from "./marfa";

export type Field = TypeDefinition["fields"][string];

// A field the form cannot show is left out, not guessed at.
export function isShown(field: Field) {
  return !["array", "object", "thumbnail"].includes(field.type);
}

function choices(field: Field) {
  if (field.type === "status") return (field.status_values ?? []).map((status) => status.value);
  return field.enum_values ?? [];
}

export function FieldControl({ name, field, isBody }: { name: string; field: Field; isBody: boolean }) {
  const label = field.label ?? name;
  const title = field.required ? `${label} *` : label;
  const info = field.description;
  switch (field.type) {
    case "boolean":
      return <Form.Checkbox id={name} title={title} label="Yes" info={info} />;
    case "date":
    case "datetime":
      return (
        <Form.DatePicker
          id={name}
          title={title}
          info={info}
          type={field.type === "date" ? Form.DatePicker.Type.Date : Form.DatePicker.Type.DateTime}
        />
      );
    case "enum":
    case "status":
      return (
        <Form.Dropdown id={name} title={title} info={info}>
          <Form.Dropdown.Item value="" title="Not set" />
          {choices(field).map((value) => (
            <Form.Dropdown.Item key={value} value={value} title={value} />
          ))}
        </Form.Dropdown>
      );
    default:
      return isBody ? (
        <Form.TextArea id={name} title={title} info={info} />
      ) : (
        <Form.TextField id={name} title={title} info={info} />
      );
  }
}
```

**A field's `label` is its name for people.** Get a type answers one for every field: the label the type gives it, else the nearest a parent type gives, else one made from the field's name. A required field gets a star, and the field's description shows as its help text.

- An `enum` field lists its values in `enum_values`.
- A `status` field lists its values in `status_values`, each with the group it belongs to.
- A type can name one field as its **body**, the long text of an item, in its display hints. The form shows that field as a larger box.
- A field the form can't draw, such as a list or an object, is left out.

[Field kinds](/catalog/field-kinds) lists every kind.

</Step>
<Step>

### Build the form from the chosen type

The command loads the types for a dropdown, then the one you pick, and draws a control for each field. Replace `src/index.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/index.tsx"
import { Action, ActionPanel, Form, popToRoot, showToast, Toast } from "@raycast/api";
import { usePromise } from "@raycast/utils";
import { useState } from "react";
import { type Field, FieldControl, isShown } from "./fields";
import { createItem, getType, listTypes, MarfaError } from "./marfa";

function toValue(field: Field, value: unknown) {
  if (value instanceof Date) {
    return field.type === "date" ? value.toISOString().slice(0, 10) : value.toISOString();
  }
  if ((field.type === "number" || field.type === "integer") && !Number.isNaN(Number(value))) {
    return Number(value);
  }
  return value;
}

export default function SaveItem() {
  const [typeId, setTypeId] = useState("core.bookmark");
  const types = usePromise(listTypes);
  const type = usePromise(getType, [typeId]);

  const fields = Object.entries(type.data?.fields ?? {}).filter(([, field]) => isShown(field));
  const bodyField = type.data?.display_hints?.body_field;

  async function save(values: Form.Values) {
    const properties: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    for (const [name, field] of fields) {
      const value = values[name];
      if (value === "" || value === false || value === undefined || value === null) continue;
      properties[name] = toValue(field, value);
    }
    try {
      const item = await createItem(typeId, properties);
      await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Success, title: "Saved", message: item.id });
      await popToRoot();
    } catch (error) {
      if (error instanceof MarfaError) {
        await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Failure, title: `Refused: ${error.code}`, message: error.message });
      } else {
        await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Failure, title: "Could not reach Marfa", message: String(error) });
      }
    }
  }

  return (
    <Form
      isLoading={types.isLoading || type.isLoading}
      actions={
        <ActionPanel>
          <Action.SubmitForm title="Save to Marfa" onSubmit={save} />
        </ActionPanel>
      }
    >
      <Form.Dropdown id="type" title="Type" value={typeId} onChange={setTypeId}>
        {(types.data ?? [])
          .filter((t) => !t.id.startsWith("system."))
          .map((t) => (
            <Form.Dropdown.Item key={t.id} value={t.id} title={t.label ?? t.id} />
          ))}
      </Form.Dropdown>
      <Form.Separator />
      {fields.map(([name, field]) => (
        <FieldControl key={`${typeId}/${name}`} name={name} field={field} isBody={name === bodyField} />
      ))}
    </Form>
  );
}
```

The dropdown leaves out the `system.` types, which Marfa writes itself. `save` skips a field left empty, so the item holds no value for it. It sends a number as a number, a `date` as a day such as `1861-08-01`, and a `datetime` as a date and time.

</Step>
<Step>

### Run it and see a refusal

Start the extension with `npm run dev`, open Raycast and search for **Save Link**. The form opens on Bookmark, with a control for each of its fields. Choose another type, and the form changes to that type's fields.

The dropdown lists every type, because any key may **read** a type's definition. Only the types in a key's access may be **written**. Your key writes bookmarks, so a book is refused. Choose **Book**, type a title, and press Command-Return. Raycast shows a toast:

```text
Refused: type_not_permitted
No access to type "core.media.book"
```

The refusal comes from the server, not from the extension. `MarfaError` kept the `code` and the `message`, and `save` showed them. The body of the refusal also names the grant the key lacks, in `details.grant`:

```json
{ "kind": "type", "name": "core.media.book", "level": "write" }
```

[Errors](/api-reference/errors) lists every code and what each one tells a program to do.

</Step>
<Step>

### Widen the key

To let the extension write books, make a new key that names both types. A source belongs to one live key, so revoke the first key before you reuse `raycast`:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa keys revoke 01a1f142-25ea-7671-bd26-35207a9efab1
marfa keys create --label "Raycast" --source raycast \
  --type-permission core.bookmark=write --type-permission core.media.book=write
```

```text
revoked key 01a1f142-25ea-7671-bd26-35207a9efab1
marfa_k1_…
key 01a1f142-fbb2-72c2-9926-0d5c748ededb (Raycast); the plaintext is shown once, keep it now
  core.bookmark    Read and edit
  core.media.book  Read and edit
```

</Terminal>

Use your own key's ID, which `marfa keys list` shows. Paste the new key into the **API Key** preference: in Raycast's settings, open **Extensions** and select Marfa Capture. Choose **Book** again and save. The **Saved** toast replaces the refusal. [Rotate a key](/run/manage-keys#rotate-a-key) covers replacing a key in more detail.

</Step>
</Steps>
